newsitem.title: UK: UK's OFT investigates holiday sales, travel agents.
newsitem.headline: UK's OFT investigates holiday sales, travel agents.

text.p: Britain's Office of Fair Trading said on Thursday that it was instigating monoplies' investigations into the supply of foreign holidays and the supply of travel agency services in relation to such holidays.

In a statement, the director general of fair trading said the reference would allow the Monopolies and Mergers Commission to look into links between large tour operators and travel agencies and some agents' practice of linking holiday discounts to the purchase of specific travel insurance.

"On ownership links, the concern is that the vertically integrated groups may be able in various ways to promote the group's own holidays at the expense of holidays of competing non-integrated tour operators and to the detriment of true consumer choice," the statement said.

OFT director John Bridgeman noted that such companies supply a large proportion of a market worth 7.0 billion pounds ($11.53 billion) and he was concerned that some of their practices could distort the competition process.

"I believe they have the market power to put competitors at a disadvantage for example by de-racking or threatening to de-rack their brochures in an attempt to negotiate larger commissions, by pressurising tour operators not to supply independent travel agents on better terms, or by pushing their own holidays through in-house incentive schemes," he said.

He said the OFT had already had prolonged discussions with two large firms, Thomson (part of Canada's Thomson Corp) and Airtours Plc, but these had not led to a satisfactory conclusion and he had opted to call in the MMC.
After the OFT statement Airtours shares plunged 64 pence, or about 9.0 percent, to 649 pence by 1055 GMT. ($1=.6072 Pound)
